title: Through Green Glass
story:
The barge moved with a lazy, deliberate rhythm, cutting quiet v-shapes into the dark water of the Grand Canal. Silas stood at the stern with one hand resting casually on the long wooden tiller, asking for nothing and offering no unnecessary words. James sat near the bow, his tail curled neatly around a wooden deck plank, feeling the gentle thrum of the timber beneath his feet. In his right hand, he held the cool, rounded triangle of sea-glass up to his left eye.

Through the glass, the cold grey cobblestones turned into the lush mossy green of the Great Canopy. Through the glass, the iron window grates softened into twining vine-paths. Through the glass, the towering stone buildings on either side of the canal lost their sharp human edges, blending into a familiar emerald haze that made James's chest feel slightly lighter.

As The Waterlily drifted deeper into Oakhaven, the narrow canal opened into a shadowy passage beneath a massive stone bridge known as the Scholar's Arch. High above, the sounds of human footsteps and carriage wheels echoed in muffled thumps against the damp masonry. Water dripped from the keystones in slow, measured drops, plinking against the canal surface like tiny brass bells.

James lowered the glass and touched the brass map canister hanging at his side. He thought of Barnaby's careful charcoal lines, remembering how the map showed these winding blue ribbons encircling the town. The canal was not just a road; it was the town's pulse, carrying timber, glass, and quiet travelers through the heart of the unknown.

The barge glided out from under the heavy vault into the soft morning sun once more. On a mossy wooden mooring post just ahead, a single white heron stood perfectly still, watching the boat approach without a flicker of fear. James held his breath as they floated past, wondering if the bird knew where the water went when the town finally ended.
location: Oakhaven, aboard The Waterlily passing under Scholar's Arch
